verifications.note: Pipeline News 'Ongoing Projects' (Oct 2018) database entry: 'Project: Revolution Pipeline ... Length: 120 miles / Diameter: 24 and 30 inches / Capacity: 440 MMcf/d', filed under ENERGY TRANSFER PARTNERS, Butler County PA.

OGJ, 'ETP provides details on Revolution Pipeline processing project': 'ETP plans to build 100 miles of high-pressure, 24-in. and 30-in. rich-gas pipeline resulting in a total gathering system capacity of more than 440 MMcfd.'

resolutions.researcher_notes: Two independent trade-press sources give 440 MMcf/d as recorded. PGJ's Oct-2018 database entry states it as an exact figure; OGJ's Feb-2018 article on ETP's announcement says 'more than 440 MMcfd' (same number, framed as a floor). Both describe the full Revolution gathering system (mainline + laterals) rather than the single 40.5-mile/24-in mainline segment that most incident coverage (PA DEP, Wikipedia, NGI) discusses — see Length note below for the scope discrepancy this reveals.

verifications.note: Pipeline News 'Ongoing Projects' (Oct 2018): 'Project: Revolution Pipeline ... Length: 120 miles', exact match to the recorded 120.00 mi.

resolutions.researcher_notes: PGJ's database entry states 120 miles exactly, matching the sheet. FLAG — a real scope discrepancy across sources, not a rounding gap: (1) OGJ (Feb 2018, ETP's own announcement) puts the planned build at '100 miles', 20 mi short of the 120 recorded/PGJ figure — plausibly PGJ's later snapshot includes laterals added after the initial announcement. (2) Separately, PA DEP's Pennsylvania Pipeline Portal, Wikipedia, and NaturalGasIntel (restart coverage, verified via curl after a 403 on WebFetch — 'the 40.5-mile pipeline') all describe 'the Revolution Pipeline' as a single 40.5-mile, 24-inch mainline between two processing facilities in Beaver/Butler/Allegheny/Washington Counties — a materially different, smaller project than the 100-120 mile/24-30in/440 MMcfd/$1.5B gathering SYSTEM that PGJ and OGJ describe. The sheet's Diameter value (24, 30 in, both sizes) only matches the PGJ/OGJ system-wide description, not the single-diameter 40.5-mi mainline sources, so P0377 as tracked appears to be modeling the full announced gathering system rather than just the mainline segment that exploded/was restarted. Only one exact-match source found for 120 mi specifically; the second independent source found (OGJ) states a different figure for the same 'system' scope. Recommend Baird confirm P0377's intended scope (full system vs. mainline-only) against the other Revolution-related rows, if any, before further edits.

verifications.note: Pipeline News 'Ongoing Projects' (Oct 2018): 'Project: Revolution Pipeline ... Diameter: 24 and 30 inches', exact match to recorded '24, 30' in.
OGJ: 'ETP plans to build 100 miles of high-pressure, 24-in. and 30-in. rich-gas pipeline', confirms both pipe sizes.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Two independent trade-press sources agree on dual 24-in/30-in construction for the gathering system, exact match to the recorded '24, 30' in. Note the single-mainline sources (PA DEP, Wikipedia, NGI) describe only a 24-inch pipe — consistent with the scope split flagged under Length: the 24-in-only mainline is a subset of this 24/30-in system.

verifications.note: OGJ: 'Overall expected capital cost for the pipeline system and associated facilities, which will be supported by long-term agreements, is about $1.5 billion, ETP said.' Exact match to recorded 1,500,000,000 USD.
Headline: 'ETP Announces $1.5B Revolution Pipeline/Plant Project in SWPA', corroborates the $1.5B figure.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Both sources trace to ETP's Feb-2018 project announcement (not two independently-derived figures), so treated as medium rather than high confidence despite being two separately-published outlets. The $1.5B figure covers 'the pipeline system and associated facilities' (i.e., pipeline + fractionation/processing plant), not the pipeline segment alone, per OGJ's own wording -- flagging as a scope caveat on SegmentCost consistent with the Length/Diameter system-vs-mainline split noted above. No later, updated actual-cost figure was found in the sources opened this pass; recommend a follow-up search of FERC/EIA cost-reporting data if a segment-only figure is wanted.
